name: Neodymium nickelate
equilibrium_context: Coupled insulator-metal and antiferromagnetic transition at about 200 K, strain-dependent in films

driven_states.emergent_property: Above-band-gap excitation first erases the magnetic order (below 180 fs); only afterwards does the insulating phase collapse (450 fs), in step with the slowest optical phonon mode. The charge order melts along with it.
driven_states.source: Stoica et al., Phys. Rev. B 106, 165104 (2022), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.106.165104
further_sources: Caviglia et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 108, 136801 (2012), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.108.136801 (mid-IR excitation of a substrate phonon mode produces, via interfacial strain, a long-lived increase of the conductivity by five orders of magnitude)
driven_states.caveat: Stoica et al. argue for a magnetically driven ordering of events (spin first), which is non-thermal. The subsequent transformation is, however, clearly first order with nucleation, growth and supercooling; the recovery is thermally and kinetically limited (Avrami). The Caviglia case is mechanistically cleanly non-thermal, because the substrate is pumped and not the sample - there, however, the final state is a strain-induced and not a photodoped metallic phase.

sources: Stoica et al., Phys. Rev. B 106, 165104 (2022), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.106.165104
Caviglia et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 108, 136801 (2012), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.108.136801
gaps: The lifetime is nucleation-limited and therefore sample-dependent.
